newsitem.title: USA: Patriot to acquire Calif. Jockey.
newsitem.headline: Patriot to acquire Calif. Jockey.

text.p: Patriot American Hospitality Inc said it has agreed to acquire California Jockey Club and Bay Meadows Operating Co, two real estate concerns whose shares are paired, for $33.00 a share in cash, or .9635 shares of Patriot.
Based on about 5.9 million shares of California Jockey and Bay Meadows, the deal is valued at $195 million, Patriot said in a statement.
The deal has been approved by the boards of directors of all three companies. If the deal is completed, Patriot plans to merge into California Jockey/Bay Meadows.

Patriot American is Dallas, Texas-based real estate investment trust (REIT) owning 42 hotels in the United States. Bay Meadows operates the Bay Meadows horse racing track near San Francisco. California Jockey is a REIT that owns the racetrack's land and other parcels around it.

"This acquisition represents a major strategic step forward for Patirot American," Paul Nussbaum, Patriot's chief executive, said in a statement. "The paired share structure provides Patriot American with multiple options for growth and greater flexibility in acquiring hotels."
Patriot American will continue racing operations at the track and build new stables using current cash.
Patriot American also will advance California Jockey/Bay Meadows a $2.9 million breakup fee to terminate a previously arranged acquisition by Hudson Bay Partners LP.
If Patriot American and California Jockey/Bay Meadows do not complete a deal, California Jockey/Bay Meadows must return the $2.9 million and pay an additional $5.0 million fee.

"We are extremely pleased with this acquisition agreement, which not only provides superior value for our shareholders, but also helps to insure the continued operation of Bay Meadows Racecourse," said Jack Liebau, Bay Meadows chief executive.
California Jockey/Bay Meadows had been talking about an acquisition or merger since this summer. Potential partners included Hudson Bay and Starwood Capital Group.

In August, Hudson Bay offered to recapitalize California Jockey/Bay Meadows with a $20 per share offer and a $300 million investment. Starwood had offered $22 a share and a $300 million investment for the company.
